title: Formalize incident-derived SLO adjustments and rollout constraints
creator: Ava Chen
background: After the February KV cache incident (postmortem link below), the incident response board proposed a set of operational mitigations and SLO adjustments. Those proposals are currently a loose list of runbook changes and engineering tasks. This ticket captures the work to convert incident action items into explicit PRD requirements: concrete SLO change language, rollout/rollback constraints, synthetic verification criteria, and acceptance tests that product and engineering can sign off on.
description: Objective: Update the Serving PRD to include incident-driven reliability constraints so future releases encode fallback behavior, SLO deviation policies, and verifiable rollout gates. Deliverables: 1) PRD section 'Incident-derived operational contracts' with exact SLO/text, 2) rollout policy language (canary thresholds, automatic rollback triggers), 3) a verification matrix (synthetic checks + telemetry criteria), 4) clear assignees and engineering dependency list.
scope_changes: Add a new non-functional requirements section to the existing Serving PRD. This will not add feature work beyond the dependencies listed; it formalizes failure-handling behavior and verification for releases touching serving/runtime, autoscaling, and KV cache logic.
acceptance_criteria: PRD contains a written SLO adjustment policy: how to change SLO targets temporarily post-incident and the approval flow (PM + ENG + SRE)
Rollout policy defined with numeric canary thresholds (error rate, p99 latency, token-per-second throughput) and automatic rollback criteria wired to alerting signals
Verification matrix included: list of synthetic checks, expected pass rates, and which checks are required before canary promotion
All engineering dependencies (ENG- keys) are referenced in PRD and owners assigned
Runbook snippets or links included for runbook-triggered rollbacks and for invoking fallback model variants
A QA plan with two synthetic test scenarios (coldstart + KV cache miss storm) and acceptance thresholds documented
Stakeholder sign-off recorded from Product, SRE, and Runtime engineering
technical_dependencies: ENG-6021 (runtime telemetry tags and alert enrichment)
notes: Trade-off: stricter rollback gates increase release friction but significantly reduce customer-visible regression windows
Decision: keep temporary SLO relaxation as an approved mitigation only with explicit timeboxed approval from SRE and PM
Follow-up: add a separate PRD addendum for Dedicated customers if the rollback semantics need to differ for reserved capacity

2025-03-01 - SRE review: requested explicit span-level tracing for fallback path, and an audit event for automatic rollback actions. PM accepted and added to acceptance criteria.

owner_notes: When writing the PRD text, use imperative language for operational contracts (e.g., 'must', 'will') and include examples. We should avoid vague language like 'consider' or 'should' for anything tied to automatic rollbacks.
qa_plan: Two synthetic scenarios are required: 1) coldstart-heavy traffic spike (simulate many new connections + KV cold misses), 2) KV cache regen storm (simulate coordinated cache invalidation). Each must meet the acceptance thresholds before canary promotion.
approval_steps: 1) Draft PRD review by Runtime ENG and SRE, 2) Address comments and update PRD, 3) PM + Eng lead sign-off, 4) Addendum included in release notes
estimated_effort_notes: PM work: 1.5 days to author + 2 review cycles. Eng work referenced separately in ENG tickets.
archival_instructions: Keep linked postmortem and PRD revisions in Confluence. When release is complete, attach release verification summary to this ticket and mark Done.
